keyword: last time we went to the moon

verifications.claim: The last time humans went to the moon was during NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Apollo 17 was the sixth and final Apollo mission to land people on the moon." (R1); "The Apollo 17 mission in 1972 marked the last time that humans walked on the moon." (R2); "the last time humans traveled to the moon." (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Apollo 17 was the last human moon mission.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission landed on the lunar surface on December 11, 1972.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: "The last U.S. astronaut to land on the moon was on Dec. 19, 1972" (R1 contradicts); "landing on the moon on Dec. 11, 1972." (R2); "landing on the Moon ... on December 11, 1972." (R5)
verifications.reasoning: R2 and R5 directly support Dec. 11 landing; R1 incorrectly attributes landing to Dec. 19 (splashdown), creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over 75 hours on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "spent about 75 hours on the Moon" (R4); "more than 73 hours were spent on the surface of the Moon." (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of ~75 hours support 'over 75 hours' precisely enough.

verifications.claim: Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt performed three moonwalks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "third moonwalk" (R2); "third and final excursion ... third Apollo 17 lunar surface extravehicular activity" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: References mention first, third, and final moonwalks/EVAs, confirming three.

verifications.claim: Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt departed on December 14, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "moonwalk ended early in the morning on Dec. 14" (R4); "stepped off the lunar surface for the last time on December 14, 1972" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of lunar departure on Dec. 14.

verifications.claim: Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt remain the last humans to walk on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "last time that humans walked on the moon" with Cernan/Schmitt (R2); "Cernan and Schmitt are still the last to walk on the Moon" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly named as last humans to walk on moon.

verifications.claim: Commander Gene Cernan was the last person to walk on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As I take man's last step from the surface ..." (Cernan speaking upon leaving)
verifications.reasoning: Cernan described taking 'man's last step' as commander.

verifications.claim: Commander Gene Cernan left on December 14, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "stepped off the lunar surface for the last time on December 14, 1972" (Cernan)
verifications.reasoning: Directly states Cernan left lunar surface Dec. 14.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct confirmations of landing site.

verifications.claim: The crew of Apollo 17 included Gene Cernan, Harrison "Jack" Schmitt, and Ronald Evans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Crew listed as Cernan, Schmitt, Evans across sources (e.g., R2: "Gene Cernan ... Harrison "Jack" Schmitt ... Ronald Evans")
verifications.reasoning: Consistently listed in all relevant sources.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "trained geologist, Harrison H. Schmitt" (R1); "Scientist-astronaut Harrison H. Schmitt" (R4)

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Ronald Evans remained in lunar orbit" (R2); "Ronald Evans remained with the Command and Service Modules in lunar orbit" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated Evans orbited while others landed.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was the longest lunar stay.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention duration (~75 hours) but no comparison stating it was the longest.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was the most productive lunar stay.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "traveled the greatest distance ... greatest number of rock and soil samples" (R1); "gathered more geology samples than any other moon mission" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Records in distance/samples imply productivity but no direct 'most productive' statement.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 covered the greatest distance with the Lunar Roving Vehicle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "traveled the greatest distance using the Lunar Roving Vehicle" (R1); "highest total distance traveled on the moon, driving a lunar rover a total of about 19 miles" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as greatest distance with rover.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 astronauts brought back 110 kilograms (242 lbs) of rock and soil samples.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "110 kilograms of rock and soil samples" (R4); "bringing 243 pounds back to Earth" (R3, ~110 kg)
verifications.reasoning: Exact mass and equivalent lbs directly match.

verifications.claim: No humans have returned to the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All sources state last moon landing/walk 1972, no returns since.
verifications.reasoning: Unanimous confirmation no human returns post-1972.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 marked the end of the Apollo program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "final Apollo mission" (R1); "the final mission in the program" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly called final mission ending Apollo.

verifications.claim: The Apollo program ended because the main goals were accomplished.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Apollo ended in 1972 – not because it failed, but because it had accomplished its task." (R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly states ended due to accomplishing goals.
